new_candidates.date_enacted: City Commission voted 4-1 to advance the ordinance on first reading 2026-09-08 (after a nearly seven-hour public hearing beginning 2026-08-31); adopted on second and final reading by a 3-2 vote 2026-09-22 (Commissioners Stokes, Langdon and Mayor Emrich in favor; Commissioners Petrow and Duval against).
new_candidates.duration: 18-month moratorium on the acceptance and approval of new data-center applications. As finally adopted, the ordinance excludes (does not apply to) the roughly 896,000-square-foot data-center facility already proposed for the Yorkshire-area 'Deep Park' development: staff may still accept, process and review that application, but the city cannot approve it without a City Commission vote. The ordinance also allows any developer to request an 'extraordinary hardship' exception (e.g., permits already issued, substantial expenditure already made), decided case-by-case by the Commission.
new_candidates.legal_basis: City of North Port ordinance (specific ordinance number not located in reviewed sources); adopted on second/final reading 2026-09-22.
new_candidates.trigger: A roughly 896,000 sq ft ('Deep Park') data-center application, part of a larger 282-acre mixed-use development, submitted 2026-07-20 after a non-disclosure agreement (entered August 2025) expired; hundreds of residents packed multiple public hearings (2026-08-31 and 2026-09-22) in opposition, citing water, noise, and infrastructure concerns.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23 (adopted the day before, 3-2); 18-month moratorium on new data-center applications, but the already-pending ~896,000 sq ft Deep Park data-center application is excluded from the pause (city staff may still process it; Commission approval is still required) rather than being retroactively swept in.
new_candidates.affected_projects: The 'Deep Park' data-center proposal: roughly 896,000 sq ft of buildings (about 123,200 sq ft of office space) on land near Yorkshire Street/Oleander Drive, part of a broader 282-acre 'employment epicenter' development; excluded from the moratorium's coverage as finally adopted.
new_candidates.outcome: 18-month moratorium adopted 3-2 on second/final reading 2026-09-22; the pending Deep Park application was excluded from coverage after the city attorney warned that including it could expose the city to litigation.

new_candidates.duration: One-year moratorium on data-center development in unincorporated Washington County (municipalities Chipley, Wausau, and Caryville are not covered, as they control their own development). A facility is defined as a data center if more than 5% of a building's gross floor area is used for computer systems/hardware/racks, in addition to an electrical-usage threshold, with anti-fragmentation language to prevent splitting a project across smaller buildings. May be extended by a further ordinance if permanent regulations are not ready in time.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Washington County ordinance (specific ordinance number not located in reviewed sources); adopted 2026-08-20.
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap; county comprehensive plan and land development code do not adequately address data-center infrastructure and public-safety impacts.

new_candidates.duration: 12-month (365-day) moratorium on accepting or processing applications for major commercial data centers, AI processing hubs, and cryptocurrency-mining operations, applying to development permits, site plans, rezonings, and conditional-use permits; exempts smaller facilities using under 50 megawatts, which may still proceed through the county's standard Special Use Permit process.

new_candidates.trigger: Concerns over water consumption from the Floridan Aquifer (including Outstanding Florida Springs Silver Springs and Rainbow Springs), power-grid strain, noise, and county staff's stated lack of readiness/criteria to evaluate large data-center applications; balanced against a proposed roughly $10 billion facility that proponents said could generate significant tax revenue and jobs.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; 12-month moratorium adopted 2026-09-15, with an exemption for facilities under 50 MW that can still apply via Special Use Permit.
new_candidates.affected_projects: An unnamed proposed data-center facility reported by proponents at the hearing as a roughly $10 billion project that could generate about $155 million in tax revenue.
new_candidates.outcome: 12-month moratorium adopted (4-1 substantive vote; 5-0 procedural adoption vote), with exemptions for sub-50-MW facilities that drew a dissenting vote from Commissioner Kathy Bryant, who opposed the carve-out.

evidence.title: Marion County approves 12-month moratorium on large-scale data centers
evidence.supports: Detailed report of the 2026-09-15 public hearing: 4-1 substantive vote (Commissioner Bryant dissenting) then 5-0 procedural adoption vote imposing a 365-day pause on large-scale data centers, AI processing hubs, and cryptocurrency mining, with a sub-50-MW exemption processed via Special Use Permit.
evidence.quote: Marion County commissioners voted on Tuesday to enact a 12-month temporary moratorium on accepting or processing applications for large-scale data centers, carving out exemptions for smaller facilities utilizing under 50 megawatts ... The vote on the motion was 4 to 1, with Commissioner Kathy Bryant the lone “no.” A subsequent procedural vote to adopt the ordinance passed unanimously 5-0.
